disease_label_per_paper: Community-acquired acute pyelonephritis with persistent CTX-M-14 ESBL-producing Escherichia coli bacteremia and ciprofloxacin treatment failure
presentation_summary: 71-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with fever for 7 days and bilateral flank pain for 2 days.
Initial vital signs were BP 176/80 mmHg, pulse 108/min, respiratory rate 25/min, and temperature 40.0 degC.

Initial labs showed WBC 20.05 x10^9/L with 91.3% neutrophils, hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, platelets 101 x10^9/L, BUN 33.2 mg/dL, creatinine 2.32 mg/dL, ESR 67 mm/hr, CRP 30.73 mg/dL, and procalcitonin 27.17 ng/mL.
Abdominopelvic CT showed diffuse swelling of both kidneys with multifocal ill-defined low-density regions compatible with acute pyelonephritis.
The next day blood and urine cultures yielded gram-negative bacilli; consecutive blood cultures later identified ESBL-producing E. coli with CTX-M-14.

risk_context.source_text_value: fever, bilateral flank pain, and CT-compatible acute pyelonephritis
no previous history of APN or prior exposure to antibiotics

observations.source_text_value: bilateral flank pain appeared two days before the visit
fever, flank pain, and CT compatible with acute pyelonephritis
bilateral renal swelling with no abscess or obstructing stone reported
no drainable abscess or obstruction was reported
no procedural source-control target was identified at presentation

imaging.finding: diffuse swelling of both kidneys with multifocal low-density regions compatible with acute pyelonephritis
imaging.source_text_value: abdominopelvic computed tomography showed diffuse swelling of both kidneys with multifocal ill-defined low density regions compatible with APN

microbiology.source_text_value: the next day, gram-negative bacilli were isolated in the two initial pairs of blood cultures and the urine culture
three days after ciprofloxacin therapy... subsequent blood cultures showed GNB again
ESBL-producing E. coli isolates were identified in all three consecutive blood samples; isolates produced CTX-M-14 type ESBL
ceftriaxone MIC >32; piperacillin-tazobactam MIC 8/4; meropenem MIC 0.06; ciprofloxacin MIC 0.25 to 0.5 but clinical failure occurred

confirmatory_findings.finding: ESBL-producing E. coli bacteremia from acute pyelonephritis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: ESBL-producing E. coli isolates were identified in all three consecutive blood samples; urine culture also grew gram-negative bacilli
The isolates produced CTX-M-14 type ESBL belonging to the ST69 clonal group

confirmatory_findings.finding: persistent bacteremia during ciprofloxacin therapy with improvement after ertapenem
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: During 3-day ciprofloxacin therapy, the patient remained febrile with persistent bacteremia; after the change to ertapenem, clinical course started to improve

actual_treatment: ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV twice daily initially
ertapenem 1 g IV once daily after persistent bacteremia

outcome.source_text_value: after the change in antibiotics to ertapenem, the patient's clinical symptoms and signs started to improve the following day

quality_warnings: This case is a post-microbiology ESBL bacteremia test: blood culture gram-negative bacteremia, ESBL phenotype, ceftriaxone non-susceptibility, and carbapenem susceptibility are rankable because they define the resistance leaf.
Treatment response and clinical improvement after ertapenem remain non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
